items.title: Earl King Interview, 1980-04-10
items.q: The interviewee mentions 'Dick' only in the context of the interviewer asking for questions for 'me or for Dick', implying Dick is a third party present or known to the group, but the interviewee provides no personal interaction or relationship details regarding Dick.

ctx.x: I mean, who he got started? Who he really produced and all that?

stuff Yeah, it wasn't from here. Joe Turner. Joe Turner. So everything that we put in the bread basket was for artists away from here. And when Dick mentioned how, how played an integral part in, with the AFO record label where they were instituting the evolvement of the 50s music is right in 60, with I know that Barbara George taking and all that stuff come out right in that era right there. Well, the transition was taking place then with the R&B sound, the bass become dominant then, you know, on the recordings…

Yeah. And then, Alice, Alice? I've always been curious as to what the record companies paid the artists in the early 50s for cutting the 45. You know, what was the, and then did you sign a contract with all those people? Well, they may have signed you. Were they really open and honest about what you were signing and all that?
